method: Preliminary comparison of user-supplied report text with the v0.4.2 coverage audit. Bibliography entries are leads, not independently verified facts. Queue entries never change evidence counts. Full source reports retained privately.

items.title: Northern Idaho — early Holocene
items.geographicScope: Pacific Northwest; Idaho requires a finer audit bin.
items.coverageAssessment: Targets the 10,000–6,000 BCE and 6,000–3,000 BCE collection gaps with named river-corridor sites. Wewukiyepuh and Kelly Forks are new locality leads; Cooper’s Ferry already has an Area B record and needs phase-level comparison rather than another counted place.
items.reviewFlags: Separate BP from cal BP and distinct occupation episodes. Older Cooper’s Ferry component dates must not overwrite the existing Area B model. A long site sequence does not establish continuous residence.

files.filename: What is the chronology and spatial distribution of Early Holocene sites in northern Idaho - Oct 29, 2026.ris

items.title: Northern Nevada and Idaho — named sites
items.geographicScope: Nevada northwestern and central/eastern basins; Pacific Northwest.
items.coverageAssessment: Directly targets the northern Nevada 10,000–6,000 BCE gap, with Crypt Cave, Leonard Rockshelter, Grass Valley and Bonneville Estates leads; also complements Idaho. Later Holocene phases remain to be resolved individually.
items.reviewFlags: Differentiate dated activity/cache evidence from habitation. Never use insect-cache or artifact counts as human population. Check revised Leonard Rockshelter chronology and explicit calibration.

files.filename: I would like a detailed list of archeolocal sites with dates of the occupation of them in northern nevada and idaho - Oct 29, 2026.ris

items.title: Aleutian occupation history
items.geographicScope: Alaska/Beringia; the chain needs dedicated dateline-aware audit coverage.
items.coverageAssessment: Provides early/middle Holocene through 1300 CE leads, complementing a broad Alaska row currently containing context but no dated locality IDs.
items.reviewFlags: The report headline extends residence across 10,000 BCE–1300 CE, but its body describes approximately 9,000-year-old earliest sites. Do not assign the query start as an occupation date or equate historical cranial categories with discrete migrating peoples.

files.filename: who lived in the aleutian islands from 10000bce to 1300 ce - Oct 29, 2026.ris

items.title: Individual Aleutian archaeological sites
items.geographicScope: Eastern, central and western Aleutian chain.
items.coverageAssessment: Anangula, Chaluka and Amaknak UNL-469 offer specific locality/phase leads; Islands of Four Mountains material may extend central-chain coverage.
items.reviewFlags: Verify individual dating, location precision and continuity claims. The existing Alaska rectangle starts at 54°N and misses much of the chain; compare both sides of the dateline before measuring this gap.

files.filename: i would like a deep dive on the archeological sites in the aleutian islands. how old how many where from whom - Oct 29, 2026.ris

items.title: Kiribati settlement and contacts
items.geographicScope: Gilbert, Phoenix and Line Islands require separate geographic treatment.
items.coverageAssessment: Targets sparse later Holocene island sequences and contacts. Te Bakoa/Nikunau is already mapped but undated because the accessed age lacks calibration; this report is a lead to recovering its original chronology.
items.reviewFlags: Do not apply one arrival date across all island groups. Island emergence is not human settlement, and broad Micronesian ancestry is not a dated local occupation. Current Marshall/Kiribati audit bounds omit islands east of the dateline.

files.filename: i would like a deep dive on the evidence for colonization of kiribati. what civilizations and when. - Oct 29, 2026.ris

items.title: Nuku Hiva and nearby Marquesan islands
items.geographicScope: Societies/Cooks/Marquesas broad row; island-level comparison needed.
items.coverageAssessment: Ho‘oumi, Hakaea and Anaho leads can refine the 1001–1500 CE cell, which already has three dated locality IDs across a much wider region; later persistence requires its own evidence.
items.reviewFlags: Retain dating disagreements and distinguish initial activity, settlement and sustained occupation. Check the reported Ho‘oumi 1129–1212 cal CE window against its original publication.

files.filename: I would like a deep dive on the colonization of Nuku Hiva and its surrounding islands - when did people get there and how long have they been there. - Oct 29, 2026.ris

items.title: Hawaiʻi settlement, trade and cultural development
items.coverageAssessment: Targets the 1001–1500 CE row currently dominated by context and the sparse later centuries. Trade, settlement and declining overseas contact need different record types.
items.reviewFlags: Keep competing arrival chronologies and source-specific date bounds; do not infer a single origin island or a precise cessation of voyaging.

files.filename: I would like a deep dive on hawaii. When did peoples get there. who did they trade with. what culture established there. Did the islands fight each other and if so when and how. was trade with far away islands disrupted and i.ris

items.title: Hawaiian raiding and kingdom consolidation
items.coverageAssessment: Adds leads for later precontact and historic warfare, competition and resource pressures rather than new settlement dots by default.
items.reviewFlags: Resource stress is a proposed causal explanation, not automatically demonstrated. Repair missing-author citations and distinguish conquest, alliance and negotiated submission.

files.filename: How did inter-island raiding, resource scarcity, and competition drive kingdom consolidation - Oct 29, 2026.ris

items.title: Hawaiian political institutions and state formation
items.geographicScope: Hawaiʻi — especially later medieval and early modern periods.
items.coverageAssessment: Targets 14th–16th-century institutional developments and later consolidation, supplementing settlement evidence with contextual political history.
items.reviewFlags: Do not project later states backward or turn a conceptual pathway into a single dated event. Check temple, agricultural and warfare chronologies separately.

files.filename: How did socio-political institutions and warfare drive state formation and inter-island conflict in Hawaiʻi - Oct 29, 2026.ris

items.title: Alaska, Yukon and northern Canadian Arctic
items.coverageAssessment: Targets Alaska’s sparse early dated-site coverage and Arctic pre-1000 CE gaps, plus revised timing of Thule expansion. Swan Point and Bluefish Caves are specific leads to reconcile.
items.reviewFlags: Separate interior histories from coastal dispersals; show disputed early evidence and differing migration chronologies. Genetics, archaeological traditions and language affiliation need independent support.

items.title: Inca report — exact repeat
items.coverageAssessment: Exact PDF duplicate of the archived round9 report. Retained for provenance; no additional gap reduction or independent corroboration.
items.reviewFlags: Revisit only for an unresolved original-source lead; do not duplicate existing round9 records.

items.title: Louisiana, Lower Mississippi and Gulf Coast — paper table
items.coverageAssessment: Twenty source leads target Louisiana and Gulf Coast settlement, chronology, fisheries, exchange and environmental context; the lower Mississippi 1000–1 BCE and 1–500 CE gaps remain open pending locality/date checking.
items.reviewFlags: Several rows are reviews or have mismatched summaries. Keep original paper metadata separate from search-generated answers.

items.title: Upper Tensas — hiatus and proposed reoccupation
items.coverageAssessment: Targets the Louisiana 1000–1 BCE gap with regional hiatus, reoccupation and mound-construction leads from Kidder, Roe and Schilling (2010).
items.reviewFlags: Interpretation of migration, not proof of complete population replacement. Sampled basin evidence cannot establish statewide absence.

items.title: Louisiana — Poverty Point, Tchefuncte and Marksville
items.coverageAssessment: Adds a regional culture-history lead spanning the query interval 1000 BCE–100 CE.
items.reviewFlags: Only a likely book review is cited. Query dates are not source-derived occupation boundaries.

items.title: Idaho — additional site inventory
items.coverageAssessment: Adds Hatwai and Hetrick leads and complements the earlier Wewukiyepuh, Kelly Forks and Cooper’s Ferry reports.
items.reviewFlags: Wewukiyepuh age is labeled cal BP in the table and BP in the body; original dating must resolve this before mapping a calendar window.

items.coverageAssessment: Adds named-site fisheries, Garden Patch feasting, pottery provenance and governance leads for the next deploy.
items.reviewFlags: Fry (1986) bibliography points to an Edzna review, not the Gulf subsistence claim. Do not generalize maize absence, egalitarian organization or continuous residence across all coastal societies.

items.title: Gulf subsistence, pottery and feasting — follow-up
items.coverageAssessment: Adds a second paper table and narrative; Bayshore Homes has two reported occupation windows to preserve separately, while Garden Patch and Shell Mound have distinct seasonal-ritual leads.
items.reviewFlags: Last table row is truncated. Gougeon entry has a mismatched summary; Middle Ohio 1300–1500 CE and southern Brazil comparison studies cannot directly support Gulf claims for 1000 BCE–1200 CE.
